packageRules.description: Renovate disables indirect (transitive) Go modules by default, so minimal-version-selection floats them up only when a direct parent bumps — leaving them below their latest supported SemVer and behind version-based advisories (OpenSSF Scorecard / OSV) that reachability-based govulncheck never flags. Track indirect deps at latest; every bump is gated by CI (build, tests, govulncheck, Trivy), so a breaking transitive update fails its PR rather than merging. To hold a specific module below latest after a genuine breakage, add a per-package rule pinning it via allowedVersions or enabled:false.

Path-versioned Go modules (…/v5, go.yaml.in/yaml/v3, gopkg.in/….v4) coexist at multiple majors, and an indirect module's major is owned by whichever upstream direct dep pins it — not by this repo. Renovate's 'major indirect' bump just rewrites the import-path major segment: the new major collides with the copy already pulled in transitively (producing a duplicate `require` directive and an invalid go.mod) or lands as an unused extra require while the old major is still needed, and it can even downgrade a sibling module. These majors advance only when the upstream consumer migrates, so suppress major indirect bumps; minor/patch indirect bumps stay enabled.

The native gomod manager tracks the go.mod `go` directive from Go releases, which can appear before the matching golang Docker image. A custom regex manager below tracks this directive from Docker Hub tags instead, so Go version PRs are created only when the builder image exists.
The custom go.mod Go directive tracker uses the Docker datasource only for tag availability. Do not try to add Docker digests to go.mod.
Keep Go version updates in lockstep: go.mod, the Dockerfile builder image, and the devcontainer image must all move together.
Keep digest-only refreshes of the Go image in lockstep across the Dockerfile and devcontainer.

Go toolchain security fixes ship as patch releases; the 7-day minimumReleaseAge would leave govulncheck failing on new stdlib advisories until it clears. Bypass the soak for Go toolchain patch/digest bumps; minor/major Go bumps still soak.

prBodyNotes: :warning: After bumping kind, run `make sync-supported-versions && make codegen` and commit the result to update `.github/supported-k8s.json` (and the generated docs). The script recomputes `supported` from the newest three kind-published minors and keeps `next` disabled as `null`. The `Verify supported-versions table` CI check will fail until this is done.

packageRules.description: The operator self-image in source install manifests is a release-managed placeholder, not a dependency Renovate should pin.
Helm publishes tarballs (and their checksums) on get.helm.sh, not as GitHub release attachments, so Renovate can only bump the version — the pinned SHA-256 must be resynced separately.
prBodyNotes: :warning: After bumping Helm, run `make sync-helm-checksum` and commit the result to update the pinned `HELM_SHA256` in `scripts/install-helm.sh`. The `Verify Helm checksum pin` CI check will fail until this is done.

customManagers.description: Track go.mod's Go directive from Docker Hub golang image tags.
Track sigs.k8s.io/kind release pin in supported-k8s.json
Track the e2e curl helper image
Track hand-pinned CLI tool versions in the Makefile
Track hand-pinned GitHub release-attachment helper binaries in install scripts (version + SHA-256 of the attachment, computed by Renovate)
Track the version-only Helm pin in install-helm.sh (tarballs live on get.helm.sh, not GitHub; the checksum is resynced via `make sync-helm-checksum`)
Track version-only devcontainer tool pins in post-install.sh
Track the version-only helm-unittest pin in install-helm-unittest.sh (per-platform archive digests live in hack/tool-checksums.txt, resynced via `make sync-tool-checksums`)
